layout.arrangement: A single white slide enclosed by a thin bright-red rectangular frame. Header row across the top: a small blue-outlined italic kicker box at top-left ('Example: Quadratic Kernel'), the large bold red title 'How to Kernelize SVM' centered, and a yellow circular badge with the slide number '36' at top-right. Below the header, a wide blue-outlined panel (upper panel) holds the original SVM dual objective on its first line, a row of two blue-outlined sub-boxes (W equation on the left, b equation on the right) on its second line, and a peach/orange-outlined 'Class of vector Z ⇒ sign(...)' strip centered beneath them. In the vertical middle of the slide sits a narrow horizontal strip: a thin red-outlined box reading 'Kernelize using' immediately followed by a red-outlined box containing the red bold formula 'K(α,b) = α^T b^2'; a red-outlined white downward arrow hangs from this strip pointing into the lower panel. The lower blue-outlined panel mirrors the upper one: kernelized dual objective on line 1, the same W box on the left and the squared b box on the right on line 2, and a peach 'Class of vector Z is sign(...)' strip on line 3. A small white mouse-pointer cursor artifact hovers over the lower b equation near the min term. A black video letterbox bar runs along the very bottom edge of the frame.

3. Place the title text 'How to Kernelize SVM' at top-center in bold red (#CC0000) sans-serif, ~28 pt.
4. Place a yellow (#FFFF99) filled circle with a thin black outline at top-right (approx. x 91%, y 13%), ~0.9 inch diameter, containing the black number '36' centered inside.
5. Draw the upper panel: a white rectangle with a thin blue (#0000CC) border spanning approx. x 7%-92%, y 18%-46%.
6. Inside the upper panel on line 1, typeset the serif math equation 'ℒ_D(α) = Σ_{i=1}^{N} α_i − 1/2 Σ_{j=1}^{N} Σ_{i=1}^{N} α_i α_j y_i y_j (X_i^T X_j)': ℒ_D in blue calligraphic, α_i in red bold, remaining symbols in black.

8. Inside the upper panel on line 2 left (approx. x 9%-25%), place a white rectangle with a thin blue (#0000CC) border containing 'W = Σ_{i=1}^{N} α_i y_i X_i': W in bold blue, α_i y_i X_i in bold red.

12. Behind 'W^T Z' inside the upper class strip, place a light-green (#CCFFCC) rounded rectangle with a green (#00CC00) outline (approx. x 40%-48%, y 39%-44%).
13. Draw the kernelization connector strip at middle (approx. x 30%-62%, y 49%-56%): a thin red (#E00000) outlined rounded rectangle with white fill.
14. Inside the left half of the connector strip, place italic black sans-serif text 'Kernelize using' (~13 pt).
15. Inside the right half of the connector strip, place a separate red (#E00000) outlined rectangle containing bold red serif math text 'K(α,b) = α^T b^2'.
16. Place a vertical downward-pointing arrow centered at approx. x 43%-45%, extending from y 47% to y 59%, with white fill and red (#E00000) outline, slim shaft with triangular head, connecting the connector strip to the lower panel.
17. Draw the lower panel: a white rectangle with a thin blue (#0000CC) border spanning approx. x 7%-92%, y 61%-91%.
18. Inside the lower panel on line 1, typeset the serif math equation 'ℒ_D(α) = Σ_{i=1}^{N} α_i − 1/2 Σ_{j=1}^{N} Σ_{i=1}^{N} α_i α_j y_i y_j (X_i^T X_j)^2' with the same color coding as step 6.
19. Behind the final term '(X_i^T X_j)^2' in the lower dual objective, place a light-green (#CCFFCC) rounded rectangle with a green (#00CC00) outline (approx. x 43%-52%, y 64%-70%).
20. Inside the lower panel on line 2 left (approx. x 9%-25%), place a white rectangle with a thin blue (#0000CC) border containing 'W = Σ_{i=1}^{N} α_i y_i X_i': W in bold blue, α_i y_i X_i in bold red.
21. Inside the lower panel on line 2 right (approx. x 34%-90%), place a white rectangle with a thin blue (#0000CC) border containing 'b = − 1/2 { max_{i,y=−1} [W^T X_i]^2 + min_{i,y=+1} [W^T X_i]^2 }': b in bold blue, max/min in red italic.
